stem: (Select TWO.) Marlowe Systems is moving state from one S3 bucket to another by editing the backend block and re-running `terraform init` in an unattended job that cannot answer prompts. Which two statements are correct?

choices.text: `terraform init -reconfigure` copies the existing state into the new bucket
A plain `terraform init` migrates the state without any prompts
`-migrate-state` makes init copy the existing state to the new location
`-force-copy` suppresses the migration prompts and also turns on `-migrate-state`
Backing up the state file before migrating is unnecessary

rationale: `-migrate-state` is the option that attempts to copy existing state to the new backend, and `-force-copy` answers yes to the migration questions, which suits an unattended job, and enables `-migrate-state` as well. `-reconfigure` does the opposite: it disregards the existing configuration and prevents migration. Re-running init on an already initialized backend needs one of those two options, and Terraform asks before migrating rather than doing it silently. The docs strongly recommend manually copying `terraform.tfstate` elsewhere before migrating, so skipping a backup is not safe.
